comparison: Both evaluate spectroscopic characterization of bathy-BphPs (C32-C42). OpenEval R5 focuses on these claims, while peer R1 combines them with pH-dependent photocycle data (C81-C94). Both find the characterization work well-supported and recognize it as a strength, with peer reviewers explicitly praising the fundamental protein characterization.

Both evaluate pH-dependent photochemical characterization (C81-C94). OpenEval notes some mechanistic aspects are speculative (C86, C95) but finds claims supported overall. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a strength with no concerns raised, describing it as revealing 'new details of the pH-dependent photocycle.'

Both evaluate the engineering strategy and screening results (C44-C47, C100). OpenEval finds the PATCHY method and variant identification well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize this as a major achievement, praising the 'modular design strategies' and engineering approach with no concerns raised.

Both evaluate flow cytometry and dose-response data (C48-C55). OpenEval finds clear NIR-light responses with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers recognize this as a major achievement, noting 'specific and tunable gene expression' with no concerns about the reported fold-changes.

Both address NIR selectivity findings (C56-C59). OpenEval finds the data supportive but notes mechanistic explanations remain speculative. Peer R2 recognizes the achievement broadly, while peer R8 and R10 raise concerns about the complexity and practical limitations of the selectivity.

Both address the unexpected selectivity and mechanistic complexity (C108-C115). OpenEval finds data supportive but mechanistic explanation speculative. Peer R8 explicitly acknowledges the complexity as difficult to rationalize but commends rigorous reporting, accepting the data despite uncertain mechanisms.

Both evaluate the mechanistic hypothesis for nonlinearity (C113-C115). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis is speculative without direct measurements. Peer R8 acknowledges the complexity as difficult to rationalize but accepts the rigorous experimental reporting.

Both evaluate orthogonal TCS systems (C60-C64). OpenEval finds proof-of-principle demonstrated despite lower efficiencies. Peer R3 explicitly highlights this as a strength and 'exciting result,' with no concerns raised about the alternative TCS implementations.

Both evaluate multiplexing capability (C65-C66). OpenEval finds proof-of-principle demonstrated. Peer R4 explicitly lists orthogonal control as a strength and 'valuable contribution,' with no concerns about the multiplexing experiments themselves.

Perfect agreement on E. coli Nissle functionality (C67-C68, C128). Both find the data well-supported. OpenEval notes comparable/improved performance. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize robust function across strains as a strength, with no concerns raised about the EcN data.

Perfect agreement on A. tumefaciens functionality (C69-C73). Both find clear light responses demonstrated. OpenEval notes differences from E. coli. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize robust function across hosts as a strength, with no concerns about the A. tumefaciens experiments.

Both address PCM modularity (C96-C97). OpenEval finds claims supported by successful engineering. Peer R7 implicitly supports this through acceptance of the overall engineering strategy and explicit recognition of 'modular design strategies' as a strength.

Both evaluate design rationale for NIR selectivity (C103-C105). OpenEval finds design rationale and validation supported. Peer R9 rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the design fully addresses limitations for all applications, particularly noting insensitivity due to rapid dark reversion.

Both address dose-response characteristics (C53-C54). OpenEval finds data clearly supportive. Peer R9 accepts the data but raises concerns about practical limitations, noting sensors are 'relatively insensitive to NIR light' which may limit downstream applications.

Both address spectral selectivity and multiplexing potential (C57-C58). OpenEval finds the selectivity data supportive. Peer R10 rates as UNCERTAIN, noting that broad Pfr responsivity makes multiplexing with blue light sensors challenging, requiring careful dosing.

Both address light response characteristics (C51). OpenEval finds clear NIR responses with appropriate controls. Peer R10 accepts the data but notes practical limitations for multiplexing with other wavelengths due to broad light responsivity.
